title: Поклонница господина Огузка  (An Admirer for Mister Oguzok)

segments.t: As the staff members grumble about sharing facilities, Kostya comes into the kitchen to tell Max that his regular older lady has arrived in the dining room again. To the amusement of the other cooks, the guest asks specifically for Max to prepare her meal.
Фу, я после него туда не пойду.
А добрый день, добрый день, дорогие друзья.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Фу, я после него туда не пойду.
'Ugh, I am not going in there after him.' Max sustains a measured manner with Kostya, combining "tuda" ("there") and "poydu" ("go") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Good afternoon to you.' Kostya presents a thoughtful stance at once, building the phrase around "dobrogo" ("good") and "dnya" ("day") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'I was simply eating.' Max keeps an easygoing manner for Kostya, leaning on "prosto" ("just") before closing the thought with "yel" ("ate").

'You should have done it the other way around.' Kostya maintains an unhurried attitude without hesitation, putting "nado" ("it is necessary") alongside "bylo" ("was") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'There is a time for everything.' Max projects a pointed bearing as they talk, weaving "vremya" ("time") together with "vsemu" ("all, whole") just the way native speakers do.
'Your retired lady friend just arrived out there.' Kostya sustains a candid approach in front of Max, joining "tam" ("there") to "pensionerka" ("pensioner") so every word pulls its weight.
А добрый день, добрый день, дорогие друзья.
'Ah, good afternoon, good afternoon, dear friends.' Max holds a warm tack in the conversation, pairing "dobryy" ("good") with "den" ("day") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Who are you filming right now?' Kostya queries evenly at this point, joining "snimayesh" ("are taking off") to "kogo" ("whom") so every word pulls its weight.
'The thing is.' Max projects a steady angle at once, building the phrase around "delo" ("matter") and "tom" ("that") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Film me instead.' Kostya strikes a clear direction straight away, building the phrase around "snimay" ("take off, remove") and "menya" ("me") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Mister Oguzok.' Max adopts a steady attitude as they talk, combining "gospodin" ("Mr, sir") and "aguzok" ("rookie, greenhorn") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Why does she only want you to cook?' Kostya challenges bluntly to Max here, linking "khochet" ("wants"), "tolko" ("only"), and "chto" ("what") in one brisk exchange.
'You guys are simply jealous of me.' Max sets an unhurried note in the conversation, pairing "prosto" ("just") with "zaviduyete" ("to envy") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Фу, я после него туда не пойду.
А добрый день, добрый день, дорогие друзья.
That wraps up this scene as while the waitresses and cooks bicker over the restroom, Kostya informs Max that the older female guest has returned and is asking specifically for him. Until next time!
